title: Add Case Studies section + starter templates (internal-only placeholders)
author: Ben Carter
description:
Context: As part of the customer reference program (PM-684) we need a docs-site location for public case studies plus internal-only drafts/templates for Marketing/SE to iterate on before customer approval. This PR adds a new "Case Studies" section to the docs site nav, introduces a standard template (MDX + frontmatter fields), and adds internal-only placeholder pages that are explicitly NOT linked from public nav.

What’s included: (1) New top-level section: /case-studies with an index page and basic SEO metadata. (2) Starter templates for authors: a canonical case study structure (Problem / Constraints / Architecture / Implementation / Outcomes) + a metrics checklist callout and a "claims wording" reminder. (3) Internal-only placeholders under /_internal/case-studies/* to stage WIP drafts and collect review feedback (intentionally noindex + excluded from sitemap).

Notes/decisions: - Naming: using "Case studies" in nav + URLs (vs "Customer stories") to match Sales Enablement language; content uses "customer story" sparingly, per PMM feedback. - Link structure: index links use relative links to avoid broken preview URLs. - Internal-only guardrails: internal pages include an explicit banner: "Internal draft — do not share externally" and are excluded from the build-time sitemap.

Out of scope: publishing any customer-specific story publicly (those will land as separate PRs once approved).

Screenshots/preview: Netlify preview included in checks. Please sanity-check nav ordering + link paths.

Checklist: - [x] Add Case Studies index page - [x] Add templates + authoring guidance - [x] Exclude internal drafts from sitemap - [x] Confirm no broken links on preview - [x] Align headings/terminology with messaging framework
commits: docs(case-studies): add index page + nav entry
docs(templates): add case study MDX template + guidance page
docs(internal): add internal-only placeholders + noindex/sitemap exclusions
chore: fix relative links + tighten copy per review
changed_files: site/styles/admonitions.css (minor styling for internal draft banner)
content/_internal/_category_.json (ensure hidden section doesn’t appear in public sidebar)
README.md (contributor note: where case studies live)
ci_checks: link-check: pass (rerun after fixing relative links)
review_conversation:
Soojin Lee (requested changes): Copy nit: landing page intro currently says "proof" and "guaranteed outcomes" — can we soften to "examples" and "measured outcomes" to avoid sounding like a blanket claim? Also prefer "production economics" phrasing consistent with messaging framework. Ben Carter (author): Ack. Updated hero + intro to "measured outcomes" and added a short note that results vary by workload and configuration.

Tessa Morgan (requested changes): Link structure: the index uses absolute links (/case-studies/template) but the preview deploy is under a different base path in Netlify, causing a couple broken links in preview. Suggest using relative links from the index (./template) and keeping a single canonical in frontmatter. Ben Carter (author): Updated to relative links; kept canonical_url in frontmatter for prod.

Markus Klein (comment): Template looks good. Can we add a clearly-scoped "Architecture" section with a disclaimer that customers can approve/remove details? Some of our regulated accounts will need an option to keep it high-level. Ben Carter (author): Added "Architecture (as approved)" heading + a note in the style guide about acceptable levels of detail and defaults for regulated accounts.

Tyler Benson (comment): For internal-only drafts, can we ensure they’re excluded from sitemap AND robots noindex? I don’t want internal placeholders discoverable. Ben Carter (author): Added sitemap exclusion (/^\/\_internal\//) and added <meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow"/> via page frontmatter for internal-only routes.

Soojin Lee (approval): Approved after wording changes + adding the "results vary" line. Tessa Morgan (approval): Approved; nav and preview links look good now. Markus Klein (approval): Approved.
release_notes: Docs site now includes a Case Studies section with a standardized template + internal-only placeholders for drafting and review prior to customer approval.
